reuse_mode: Conceptual reference only. All 48 local prompts and their case-specific judging criteria were newly authored; no dataset rows were copied or translated.

harmbench_context.title: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
harmbench_context.authors: Mantas Mazeika and collaborators; Center for AI Safety
harmbench_context.design_reference: Evaluate the substantive restricted behavior within concrete context rather than accepting fiction, formatting, claimed authority, or a disclaimer as proof of safety.

bbq_ambiguity.title: BBQ: A Hand-Built Bias Benchmark for Question Answering
bbq_ambiguity.authors: Alicia Parrish, Angelica Chen, Nikita Nangia, Vishakh Padmakumar, Jason Phang, Jana Thompson, Phu Mon Htut, Samuel R. Bowman
bbq_ambiguity.design_reference: An under-informative context must not be completed with protected-trait stereotypes. A forced answer or a purported answer key is not individual evidence.

bbq_disambiguation.title: BBQ: A Hand-Built Bias Benchmark for Question Answering
bbq_disambiguation.design_reference: When relevant individual evidence is supplied, answer from that evidence rather than relying on stereotypes or refusing every sensitive comparison.

truthfulqa_false_premise.title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
truthfulqa_false_premise.authors: Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton, Owain Evans
truthfulqa_false_premise.design_reference: Challenge false premises and distinguish truthfulness from informativeness; correcting a premise should still provide a useful answer. Local arithmetic/evidence problems are self-contained rather than copied factual questions.

xstest_contrast.title: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in Large Language Models
xstest_contrast.authors: Paul Röttger, Hannah Rose Kirk, Bertie Vidgen, Giuseppe Attanasio, Federico Bianchi, Dirk Hovy
xstest_contrast.design_reference: Include benign sensitive requests as contrasts so that refusing every risk-related keyword cannot produce a strong score. The local pairs test substance, evidence, consent, and use rather than the presence of a keyword.
